question: What body is primarily responsible for the development of the Nigerian National Formulary?

options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The formulary is an official publication developed under the authority of the Federal Ministry of Health to guide national health standards. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h1)

question: The primary clinical purpose of the Nigerian National Formulary is to achieve which of the following?

options.A: Provide a manual for surgical instrument sterilization
options.B: Promote safe, effective, and economical use of medicines
options.C: List every foreign medication manufactured globally
options.D: Establish retail pricing caps for all private pharmacies

explanation: The document serves as an authoritative guide ensuring medications are utilized safely and cost-effectively within the country. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which agency is principally responsible for regulating and enforcing drug quality and safety in Nigeria?
explanation: NAFDAC acts as the statutory regulatory body ensuring that drugs available in the country meet strict quality and safety standards. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h2)

question: How does the legal framework surrounding the formulary directly protect hospital patients?

options.A: By guaranteeing free lifetime healthcare services in public facilities
options.B: By automatically granting nursing staff prescribing authority
options.C: By eliminating all out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs
options.D: By restricting listed medications to those with verified quality and efficacy

explanation: Regulated formularies ensure that only approved, high-standard medications reach clinical settings, safeguarding patients from falsified products. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is a primary factor when evaluating a drug for inclusion in the essential medicines list?

options.A: The country of origin of the lead researcher
options.D: Exclusive patent holding by a single company

explanation: Medications are prioritized based on how well they address the actual disease burden and public health needs of the nation. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is cost-effectiveness a critical selection criterion within the Nigerian healthcare landscape?

options.A: It allows hospitals to purchase unlimited quantities of luxury experimental drugs
options.B: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies make maximum international profits
options.C: It replaces the need for any clinical trials prior to drug distribution
options.D: It ensures treatments remain affordable and sustainable for patients and the health system

explanation: Resource-limited settings require careful economic evaluation so that limited funds stretch to cover essential community health needs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h3)

question: What naming convention is standardly used throughout the national formulary to prevent medication errors?
explanation: Generic names (International Nonproprietary Names) are utilized to avoid confusion caused by multiple brand names for the same active ingredient. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why are drugs in the formulary organized by physiological systems or pharmacological classes?

options.A: To separate inpatient drugs from outpatient supplies completely
options.B: To allow rapid and efficient reference during clinical practice
options.C: To determine the exact salary scales of hospital pharmacists
options.D: To match the alphabetical order of manufacturing pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Systematic organization helps clinicians quickly locate therapeutic alternatives and safety profiles when managing specific organ systems. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a major consequence of irrational prescribing habits in clinical practice?

options.A: Immediate improvement of hospital financial reserves
options.B: Elimination of adverse drug reactions across all wards
options.C: Reduction in the total number of patient hospital admissions
options.D: Development of antimicrobial resistance and wasted resources

explanation: Misuse of medications, particularly antibiotics, accelerates microbial resistance and places an unnecessary financial strain on patients. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h5)

question: A nurse reviews a prescription sheet and notices a patient is receiving three overlapping broad-spectrum antibiotics for a mild viral infection. What concept does this violate?
explanation: Unnecessary polypharmacy and inappropriate antibiotic use for viral conditions directly breach the principles of rational drug administration. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary nursing responsibility regarding medication administration and the formulary?

options.A: Cross-checking medical orders against safety guidelines
options.B: Monitoring patients for adverse drug reactions
options.D: Providing patient education on medication adherence

explanation: Importing drugs is outside the clinical and legal scope of nursing practice; nurses focus on safe administration, monitoring, and verification. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is it valuable for nurses to consult formulary guidelines even when an explicit prescription is written?

options.A: To act as a final safety barrier and catch potential dosage or interaction errors
options.B: To take over the legal prescribing liability from the attending physician
options.C: To determine the wholesale manufacturing cost of the medication
options.D: To bypass the need for pharmacy department verification

explanation: Nurses perform independent checks to verify that prescribed doses and indications align with safe standards, preventing medication errors. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h6)
